title: Cuzzupe Calabresi
author: Marco Bellini
desc: Calabria's own braided Easter cookies, their dough shaped into decorative rings or braids around whole hard-boiled eggs, a simpler, crunchier cousin to Cuddura cu l'Ova.
longDesc: While cuddura is a soft yeasted bread, cuzzupe are firmer, cookie-like, and unleavened by comparison, their glossy egg-wash finish and colorful sprinkles making them a favorite for Calabrian children to help decorate each Easter.
ingredients: Hard-boiled eggs, in their shells, for decorating
steps: Cream the butter and sugar together until light.
Beat in the 3 eggs and lemon zest.
Combine the flour, baking powder, and salt, then fold into the wet ingredients to form a firm, workable dough.
Rest the dough, covered, for 30 minutes.
Divide into portions and shape into ropes, braiding or coiling them into rings or decorative shapes.
Nestle a hard-boiled egg into each shape, securing gently with a bit of extra dough if needed.
Brush with beaten egg and scatter with colorful sprinkles.
Bake at 180C (350F) for 20-25 minutes until golden.
chefTips: The dough should be firm enough to hold decorative shapes like braids and rings without spreading.
These are traditionally a fun, hands-on project for children to help shape and decorate.
Securing the eggs well prevents them from shifting during baking.
commonMistakes: Making the dough too soft, causing the decorative shapes to lose definition during baking.
Not securing the eggs well, allowing them to roll out of position.
Skipping the egg wash, which is what gives the finished cookies their glossy sheen.
servedWith: As part of an Easter breakfast or holiday table
storage: Store wrapped at room temperature for up to 4 days.
reheating: Not applicable; served at room temperature.
healthBenefits: A good source of protein from the eggs.
culturalNote: Cuzzupe are a beloved Calabrian Easter tradition, their firm, cookie-like texture and playful decorative shapes making them a favorite for children to help create each spring.
